title: Lock exposure for scene-light dimming validation
objective: Investigate and fix why the environment looks similarly bright across --scene-light-intensity-scale values by adding launch-time exposure/eye-adaptation control to the flashlight entry points.
instructions: Investigate the likely cause that Unreal auto exposure / eye adaptation keeps perceived brightness similar even when existing scene lights are scaled.

Add a launch-time CLI control to disable or lock auto exposure for both examples/flashlight/run.py and examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py, using existing config patterns where possible. Prefer conservative names such as --disable-auto-exposure defaulting on for flashlight validation only if safe; otherwise expose explicit --disable-auto-exposure / --enable-auto-exposure flags with a clear default.
Ensure the scene-light scaling still happens before spawning the co-located flashlight and that the flashlight intensity is not scaled.
If feasible without launching Unreal, add validation tests for new argument defaults/invalid values and update README with commands comparing --scene-light-intensity-scale under fixed exposure.
Do not create commits or perform Git operations. Return exact verification commands/results and exact user validation commands.
expected_outputs: Diagnosis, changed files, tests/verification, and commands to validate brightness changes at scene-light scales 0.2, 0.1, and 0.0.
definition_of_done: The flashlight entry points expose a documented way to prevent exposure adaptation from masking scene-light scale changes, with tests/docs updated and no commit created.
